newsitem.title: UK: Technicals tip off correction in European bonds.
newsitem.headline: Technicals tip off correction in European bonds.

text.p: European bond markets are approaching overbought levels and need of a correction before they go on to forge new highs, technical analysts said on Tuesday.
Out of the major European markets, Bunds and notionnel look the most positive on a technical basis, they added, while BTPs' recent hefty rise is starting to look overdone.
"The indications are that markets are beginning to lose a bit of momentum to the upside, things are getting overbought," said Richard Adcock, technical research manager at HSBC Futures here.
"It's been a good run, and that move will likely be extended over the long term, but shorter term it looks like some profit taking is coming through."
European bond markets have surged over the last week or so, feeding off renewed hopes that European Monetary Union will go ahead on time.

The September BTP contract spiked to a new all-time high on Tuesday at 132.67, before paring its gains. The notionnel rose to 129.38, just 48 basis points shy of its contract high, and September Bunds briefly touched their contract high at 101.88 before slipping back to 101.55.

Brenda Sullivan, technical analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London, said European markets had met their upside objectives and that divergence indicators suggested any further near term gains would be limited.
"So I expect a very short term setback...to test key supports that are very close to where we are, such as steep uptrends or previous break points," she said.
Sullivan said the next couple of days would be crucial in determining future direction.
"If those (key supports) hold in the next few days, we can go to the next high levels, but if they break, we will move down to retracement areas and congestion levels," she said.
Sullivan said intra-day divergences in September BTPs suggested a retreat to 132.03 and possibly key support at 131.80. By 1105 GMT, BTPs were up four basis points at 132.22.
"A break of this area of minor congestion and previous resistance signals retreat to the 131.10," she said.
But a break to the upside through 132.79 -- though unlikely -- could see wave extensions to 133.67 and possibly toward 135.09, she added.
Robin Wilkin, senior technical analyst at MCM YieldWatch in London, said Bunds had some limited upside potential, but would soon pull back.
"There is potential for a near term push higher but I am really looking for either yesterday's high at 101.87 or 101.99, the previous high on February 27, to cap the market," he said.
He said he was looking for a pull back initially towards 101.28, the 50 percent retracement of the current rally from 100.69 to 101.87.

"Daily studies are a little bit overbought but there is no real evidence of a short-term top forming yet and until I see that I wouldn't really want to call 100.90 yet, but underneath 101.14 there is that level," said Wilkin.

HSBC's Adcock said Bunds and notionnel looked to be fairly evenly matched in terms of technicals. "But BTPs have had a very good run and we do need to see some more prolonged consolidation there," he said.
